newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil barge premiums slip, volume dwindles.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil barge premiums slip, volume dwindles.

text.p: Colder weather in Europe failed to bring out the bulls on the NWE gas oil market on Tuesday and muted demand and ample immediate stocks helped push heating oil barge premiums lower, traders said.
Dec IPE futures finished at $3 firmer at $221.50 a tonne due to the chillier temperatures and arrival of snow in some places.
But heating oil barges premiums sagged, with trades done at Dec IPE +$3, $2.50 and $2.25, between $1 and $2 lower.

Barge trade was thin, partly because traders could not find vessels and partly because players wanted to stay out of the market to protect themselves against potential price swings from the delivery of the record high 865,100 tonne November IPE expiry. The delivery has absorbed almost all available Rotterdam barge capacity.

A barge of low suplhur diesel was traded unchanged at Dec IPE +$13 basis Flushing for late November. On the cargo market, heating oil was offered at Dec Ipe +$5/6 and bid at $3/4, around $1 lower than the morning with demand continuing thin.
